headline_marked: [[Messi scores 100th goal]], leads Inter Miami to Campeones Cup glory
headline: Messi scores 100th goal, leads Inter Miami to Campeones Cup glory
summary: Lionel Messi headed a goal and provided an assist as Inter Miami secured a 2-0 victory over Cruz Azul in the annual Campeones Cup. This triumph marks Inter Miami's first-ever win in the competition.
details: Lionel Messi showcased his brilliance by scoring a header and providing an assist, guiding Inter Miami to a 2-0 victory over Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup. This win marks the club's inaugural triumph in the annual clash between Major League Soccer and Mexican Liga MX champions.
The Argentine superstar's goal was his 100th for Inter Miami, a significant milestone. The victory was sealed when Casemiro headed home a late corner from Messi, securing the two-goal cushion.

This trophy is Messi's first of the year, coming two months after Argentina's heartbreak in the 2026 World Cup final. It also marked a winning debut for new head coach Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez, who took charge of his first game for Miami after visa delays.
Miami's opening goal came in the 24th minute, a rare header from Messi. Luis Suarez delivered a cross from the byline, and the 5-foot-7 Messi outjumped Willer Ditta to nod the ball into the net.

Suarez nearly set up another goal in the 32nd minute, receiving a cross-field pass from Messi and setting up German Berterame, whose effort was cleared off the line. Early in the second half, Messi had a goal disallowed for offside.

Cruz Azul had several opportunities, including Jose Paradela's early shot saved by Miami goalkeeper Dayne St Clair and a glancing header by Gabriel Fernandez that hit the post in the 67th minute. However, Miami's defense held firm.

The Campeones Cup is an annual event pitting the previous year's MLS Cup winner against Mexico's Campeon de Campeones winner. This was the eighth edition of the cup, always hosted by the MLS participant.
Mexican teams had won the three most recent editions before Miami's victory. Despite their status as Mexican giants, Cruz Azul has never won the Campeones Cup, having also lost the 2021 final.

headline_marked: Australia to [[bar foreign students from bringing partners, children]] as migration rules tighten
headline: Australia to bar foreign students from bringing partners, children as migration rules tighten
summary: The new policy aims to significantly reduce net overseas migration to 225,000 by 2028, a move that follows concerns over housing and infrastructure strain.
details: Australia is set to prevent foreign students from bringing their partners and children to the country while they study, alongside tightening visa rules for temporary migrants. This significant policy shift aims to curb the nation's soaring migration numbers.

Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke is expected to announce that net overseas migration will be reduced to 225,000 by 2028, a substantial decrease from the current figure of approximately 300,000. This measure is part of a broader strategy to manage population growth.

Currently, international students' spouses and partners are permitted to work in Australia, with varying hour limits based on the student's course. Students can also bring dependent children under 18 years of age.

The government's decision comes amidst pressure from the hard-right One Nation party, which has advocated for drastic cuts to temporary migration. The party's "Australia first" approach seeks to provide "breathing space" for Australians.

Australia's migration intake surged after borders reopened in February 2022 following COVID-19 restrictions, driven largely by international students and skilled workers. Critics argue this influx has strained housing, infrastructure, and social cohesion.

Official data shows net overseas migration peaked at 518,000 in 2023, then decreased to 429,000 in 2024. For the year ending June 30, 2025, it totaled 306,000, with international students comprising over half of that figure.
